title: Implement all open issues by lane in stacked PRs

intent.outcome: Starting from current master, implement GitHub issues #2722, #2740, #2748, #2749, #2750, #2752, #2753, #2754, and #2755 as dependency-ordered stacked pull requests grouped by coherent lane.
non_goals: Do not merge the pull requests or weaken independent review authority.
Do not add parallel caches, ledgers, proof registries, or GitHub-specific authority to provider-neutral core.
Do not absorb adjacent closed issues except where their existing contracts are reused by the open issue acceptance criteria.

parent.contribution: Close the entire current open backlog through one reviewable stack.
parent.closure_boundary: All nine issues have implemented, validated, pushed PR lanes with correct stack bases and truthful closeout.

owned: Lane 1: #2722, #2740, and #2753 bounded output, projection reuse, and configured target identity.
Lane 2: #2748 and #2750 proof admission binding and proof-evidence fixed-point freshness.
Lane 3: #2752 and #2754 residue reconciliation and bounded external-effect Planning routing.
Lane 4: #2749 locally reproducible packed-artifact validation using existing conformance authority.
Lane 5: #2755 complete freshness-bounded PR review intake without independent-review authority.
Focused fixtures, generated projections, documentation, workflow wiring, and maintained dogfooding evidence required by those issues.
effects: Modify repository source, tests, contracts, generated surfaces, workflows, and planning evidence required by the nine issues.
Create and push one branch and pull request per lane, with each PR based on the previous lane branch.
Reference and close the owned issues from the appropriate PR bodies while leaving PR merge to reviewers.

refs: Focused regression tests named by each issue
Hosted checks on every pushed PR head
No open PRs at task start

next_action: Implement and publish lane 2 for #2748 and #2750 on PR #2756, then continue lane 3 from the lane 2 head.
blockers: None. Escalate if an issue requires changing an authority boundary or cannot satisfy its maintained replay without redesign beyond this stack.

claims: Each issue's ordinary-path intended outcome and acceptance criteria are implemented rather than documented around.
Each lane is independently reviewable and its PR base expresses the actual stack dependency.
The final stack preserves fail-closed authority, proof freshness, bounded output, and low-residue behavior.
requirements: Add failing-before/passing-after fixtures for every issue reproduction and named counterexample.
Run the routed implement/proof command with the exact changed paths for each lane.
Run focused tests before each commit and workspace-wide lint, typecheck, and tests before final handoff.
Inspect hosted checks and all review surfaces before claiming the stack ready for review.
refs: Lane 1 focused config/correction tests and generated Python/TypeScript adapter conformance passed

continuation.owner: Codex until all lane PRs are published and checked; reviewer/maintainer afterward
continuation.residual_intent: PR review and merge in stack order only

ask_before: Adding a new top-level command or durable authority surface
Merging or force-pushing a PR branch
stop_conditions: A maintained reproduction contradicts an issue's stated intended outcome
A lane cannot be kept independently testable or safely stacked
Hosted authentication or permissions prevent branch/PR publication
